title: Finite over a locally Noetherian base is finitely presented
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and
let $p:T\to S$ be a
finite morphism. Then $p$
is of finite presentation.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft], finiteness implies that $p$ is locally of finite type. A finite morphism is affine by the finite-morphism convention in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3).
Apply [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] to the locally finite type morphism $p$ and the locally Noetherian target $S$ to obtain that $p$ is locally of finite presentation.
A morphism that is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated is of finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Combining Steps 1 and 2 proves the claim.
